items.title: Ronaldo let Manchester United down - Ten Hag
items.summary: Ten Hag says Ronaldo did not complete post-match run Former manager claims club broke promises made to him Erik ten Hag has claimed Cristiano Ronaldo “let the team down” during their time together at Manchester United. Ten Hag has also alleged that promises made by United’s owners went unfulfilled, leading to his sacking by the club in October 2024 . Ronaldo returned for a second spell at United in August 2021 and was already at the club when Ten Hag was appointed in April 2022 as Ole Gunnar Solskjær’s successor .

items.title: Haaland a doubt, Semenyo out - what are Man City's options?
items.summary: Ghana forward sustained knee injury against Ipswich Maresca to ring changes against AEK Athens on Tuesday Antoine Semenyo has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury, leaving Enzo Maresca short of alternatives to Erling Haaland, who is a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League game at home against AEK Athens on Tuesday. Semenyo limped off against Ipswich on Saturday and Haaland hobbled off at full time with a foot injury. City are eager to get their European campaign back on track after losing against Paris Saint-Germain last Wednesday.

items.title: Man Utd showed 'unity' in draw with Leeds - Carrick
items.summary: Head coach insists ‘we can still have a really good season’ ‘We were the dominant side,’ says Leeds manager Farke After a week in which Michael Carrick had “the headphones on” to quieten the noise, the Manchester United head coach claimed his side’s 1-1 draw at Leeds on Sunday “felt like a fresh start” and insisted that the season can still be a good one. Carrick’s team have seven points from seven Premier League games and have won only once in the competition, against Ipswich in August. Sunday’s draw followed the previous weekend’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham .

items.title: Animal rights group urges Crystal Palace to retire bald eagle mascot
items.summary: Peta calls on club to never again use a live animal mascot ‘There’s no reason to drag a wild animal into a stadium’ A leading animal rights group has urged Crystal Palace to retire their American bald eagle mascot because, it says, the matchday experience can leave the bird “frightened, disoriented and panicked” and put spectators at risk. In a letter to Palace’s chief executive, Sharon Lacey, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) called on the club to end Phoenix’s appearances at Selhurst Park and commit never to use a live animal mascot again.

It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. items.title: Football Australia chair Anter Isaac dismisses recent Fifa ructions as ‘growing pains’
items.summary: Isaac appears to back current direction of world governing body But ‘premature’ to talk about support for Gianni Infantino Football Australia chair Anter Isaac has played down concerns around the controversial World Cup privatisation push engineered by Gianni Infantino ahead of a meeting of Asian confederation officials in Tokyo this week. Isaac’s sentiments come amid a global rebound in support for the embattled Fifa president, who at one stage appeared unlikely to be able to continue in his role following criticism led by officials in Europe and North America .

items.title: ‘Like a family’: De Zerbi credits players’ talk and bonding trip for improving Tottenham
items.summary: Spurs off bottom after first win against Coventry Lampard unhappy Marmoush goal stood Roberto De Zerbi said that Tottenham are playing with more togetherness after holding a clear-the-air meeting before their recent game with Manchester United. Spurs went on to draw 1-1 with 10 men against United and are out of the bottom three after beating Coventry 3-1 at home on Monday night. De Zerbi felt the performance against Coventry could have been better but was happy with his side’s attitude as they claimed their first Premier League win of the season.

items.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
items.summary: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election.
